* I'rab:
(إليّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحي), and (الهاء) in (أنّه) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of أنّ; (من الجنّ) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نفر) ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أوحي ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «استمع نفر ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه استمع ...) is in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb أوحي.
The clause «قالوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause استمع. The clause «إنّا سمعنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, object of the saying.
The clause «سمعنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
2- (إلى الرشد) attached to (يهدي), (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (به) attached to (آمنّا), (الواو) conjunction; (بربّنا) attached to (نشرك).
The clause «يهدى ...» is in the position of an accusative, naʿt of (قرآنا) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) of (قرآنا), which is qualified by (عجبا).]. The clause «آمنّا ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause سمعنا.
The clause «لن نشرك ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause آمنّا.
3- (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; (صاحبة) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the first object being implied (muqaddar), i.e. a woman ...; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (ولدا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to صاحبة [Note: In the speech there is something implied, i.e. "nor anyone as a child".] ...
The clause «تعالى جدّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication [Note: The clause may be the khabar of (أنّ), and the clause after it a ḥāl of ربّنا.].
The clause «ما اتّخذ ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ). The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه ... ما اتّخذ) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the position of the pronoun in (به), i.e. "we believed in it" [Note: In these verses (أنّ) comes with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa ... so the interpreted maṣdar in them is conjoined to the position of the pronoun in (به), despite the preposition not being repeated; but the omission is regular in this construction beginning with (أنّ).].
4- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّه كان ...) like أنّه استمع, and the noun of (كان) is the pronoun of the matter, omitted [Note: Or an obligatorily latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the following سفيه, because the verb يقول contends with it for it (tanāzuʿ).], (على الله) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of يقول, i.e. "the fool says, lying against Allah"; (شططا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), being its adjective, i.e. an outrageous saying [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه ... ما اتّخذ). The clause «كان يقول ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the third (أنّ).
The clause «يقول سفيهنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كان ...
5- (الواو) conjunction; (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter, omitted; (على الله) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of تقول; (كذبا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, i.e. a lying saying.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا ظنّنا) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar أنّه كان ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن تقول) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّنا.
The clause «ظننا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the fourth (أنّ).
The clause «لن تقول الإنس ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
6- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّه كان ...) like the previous; (من الإنس) attached to a naʿt of (رجال); (برجال) attached to (يعوذون), (من الجنّ) attached to a naʿt of the second (رجال); (الفاء) conjunction; (رهقا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «كان رجال ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «يعوذون ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كان.
The clause «زادوهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause كان رجال.
7- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّهم ظنّوا) like أنّا ظنّنا; (ما) maṣdar particle; (أن لن يبعث ...) like أن لن تقول ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم ظنّوا) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان..)
The interpreted maṣdar (ما ظننتم) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a supposing like your supposing".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن يبعث) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّوا — or of ظننتم — [Note: The other two objects of supposing are omitted, indicated by the maṣdar standing in their place with the other verb of supposing.].
The clause «ظنّوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «ظننتم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لن يبعث الله ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
8- (الواو) conjunction; (الفاء) likewise; (حرسا) tamyīz (specification), accusative [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi, according to those who make the verb ملأ transitive to two objects.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا لمسنا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «لمسنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «وجدناها ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لمسنا.
The clause «ملئت ...» is in the position of an accusative, second mafʿūl bihi of (وجدناها).
9- (الواو) conjunction; (منها) attached to a ḥāl of مقاعد [Translator's note: the source reads «بحب», evidently a misprint for «بحال».] [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb نقعد, by making it include the meaning of نتّخذ.], (مقاعد) mafʿūl muṭlaq [Note: For it is the plural of the mīmī maṣdar مقعد ... Or it is a mafʿūl bihi of the verb نقعد, by the inclusion of meaning mentioned above, and مقاعد is the plural of the noun of place مقعد.], accusative, i.e. sittings for listening; (للسمع) attached to (نقعد) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt of مقاعد.], i.e. for the sake of listening; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) jussivising conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (يستمع) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents; (الآن) adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative, attached to (يستمع), (له) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا كنّا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «كنّا نقعد ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «نقعد ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كنّا.
The clause «من يستمع ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يستمع ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «يجد ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «جد ربنا» there is a metaphor from الجدّ meaning power and fortune, because kings and the rich are the fortunate (majdūdūn). The meaning: He is described as exalted above having a consort or a child because of His majesty, or because of His authority and dominion, or because of His self-sufficiency.
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وأنا لمسنا السماء».
I.e. we sought to reach it to listen to the speech of its inhabitants, or we sought its news. As for اللمس, it has been said: it is borrowed from المسّ (touching) for seeking, like الجسّ (feeling). One says لمسه, التمسه and تلمسه, like طلبه, اطلبه and تطلبه. What is apparent is that the metaphor is lexical, because it is a majāz mursal, being used for what its meaning entails.

* Benefits:
- Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ see the jinn?
The narrators differed as to whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the jinn. Ibn Masʿūd affirmed it, in what Muslim narrated from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and his ḥadīth has preceded in Sūrat al-Aḥqāf, at the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن». Ibn ʿAbbās denied it, in what al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated from him. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ. The devils had been barred from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. So the devils returned to their people, who said: What is the matter with you? It was said: We have been barred from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us. They said:
That is only because of something that has happened; so travel through the east and the west of the earth and look for the cause.
So they set out, and the group that took the direction of (Tihāma) passed by the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Nakhla, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ, as he was leading the Companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur'an and listened to it, they said: This is what has barred us from the news of heaven. So they returned to their people and said: O our people, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an that guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse to His Messenger ﷺ. As for the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd, it is another incident and other jinn. The upshot of the Book and the Sunna is the definitive knowledge that the jinn and devils exist and are bound by the rulings of the Sharīʿa, and that he ﷺ is a messenger to humans and jinn.
- Miracles of the prophets [Translator's note: the heading reads «كرامات الأنبياء»; the discussion that follows concerns the karāmāt (marvels) of the saints (awliyāʾ).]:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: In this verse there is a proof of the invalidity of karāmāt, because those to whom karāmāt are ascribed, even if they are approved saints, are not messengers; and Allah has singled out the messengers — from among those approved — for being shown the unseen. In it there is also the invalidation of soothsaying and astrology, because their practitioners are the furthest of all from being approved and the most deeply in displeasure. Al-Wāḥidī said: In this there is proof that whoever claims that the stars indicate to him what will be, of life or death and the like, has disbelieved in what is in the Qur'an.
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he denied the karāmāt of the saints, in keeping with the principle of his Muʿtazilī school, and he agreed with al-Wāḥidī and other exegetes on the invalidity of soothsaying and astrology. Imām Fakhr al-Dīn said: The relation of the verse to the two cases is the same; if the verse is made to indicate the prohibition of astrological judgements, then it ought to be made to indicate the prohibition of karāmāt. He said: In my view the verse indicates nothing of that. What it indicates is that His saying (فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا) contains no form of generality; so it is enough, in acting upon what it requires, that Allah the Exalted not reveal to His creation one particular unseen matter among His unseen matters. So it is taken to refer to the time of the occurrence of the Resurrection, and the meaning of the verse is that He, the Exalted, does not reveal this unseen matter to anyone; so there remains in the verse no indication that He does not reveal anything of the unseen to anyone. Moreover, it is permissible that Allah should show something of the unseen to others than the messengers. What is fitting is that the school of Ahl al-Sunna affirms the karāmāt of the saints, contrary to the Muʿtazila, and that it is permissible that Allah should inspire some of His saints with the occurrence of certain events in the future, and they then inform of it. What indicates the soundness of that is what
was narrated from Abū Hurayra — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Among the nations before you there were people who were spoken to (muḥaddathūn), inspired.
And from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to say: There used to be among the nations before you people who were spoken to; if there is any of them in my nation, then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb is one of them.
In this there is an affirmation of the karāmāt of the saints. Whatever may be a miracle (muʿjiza) for a prophet may validly be a karāma for a saint. The difference between them is that the miracle is something that breaks the norm, coupled with a challenge (taḥaddī), and it is not permissible for a saint to claim the breaking of the norm along with a challenge, for if a saint claimed it he would disbelieve that very moment. As for soothsaying, its door was closed with his ﷺ being sent; so whoever claims it is a disbeliever. And Allah the Exalted knows best.
10- (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (شرّ) fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation), its implied form being "حصل" or "تمّ" [Note: (شرّ) may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أريد; in that case the verbal clause أراد is conjoined to the nominal clause شرّ أريد.]. (بمن) attached to (أريد), (أم) conjunction [Note: The clause after it is interpreted as a single word; therefore it is valid for it to be a conjunction, i.e. "is evil intended for those on earth, or good?", and (خير) was expressed by a clause ... It may also be disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning بل, in which case the clause after it is resumptive.], (بهم) attached to (أراد) ... and (في الأرض) attached to the ṣila of من ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا لا ندري ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «لا ندري ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «(أحصل) شرّ ...» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the object of ندري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «أريد ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «أراد بهم ربّهم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the implied clause حصل.
11- (الواو) conjunction; (منّا) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الصالحون), and likewise the second (منّا); the mubtadaʾ is implied, qualified by the adverb دون, i.e. "among us are people below that" [Note: According to the view of al-Akhfash, (دون) is a word meaning غير, indeclinable because it is annexed to an indeclinable word, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ.], (طرائق) khabar of كنّا, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "people of ways" [Note: The omission of the muḍāf may be in the noun of كان, i.e. "our states were ways" ...].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا منّا الصالحون) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding maṣdar.
The clause «منّا الصالحون ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «منّا دون ذلك ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «كنّا طرائق ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or causal.
12- (الواو) conjunction; (أن لن نعجز..) like أن لن تقول..; (في الأرض) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of نعجز; (هربا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "fleeing"..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا ظننّا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن نعجز) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّنا.
The clause «ظنّنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «لن نعجز ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
The clause «لن نعجزه ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause نعجز.
13- (الواو) conjunction; (لمّا) adverb meaning "when", including the meaning of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the answer آمنّا; (به) attached to (آمنّا), (الفاء) resumptive; (من يؤمن) like من يستمع; (بربّه) attached to (يؤمن), (الفاء) linking to the answer of the condition; (لا) negative, and the second is redundant, to emphasise the negation; (رهقا) conjoined to (بخسا), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا لمّا سمعنا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding maṣdar.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its answer ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «سمعنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آمنّا به ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition.
The clause «من يؤمن ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive and causal.
The clause «يؤمن بربّه ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «لا يخاف ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو"; and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive, the answer of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
14- (الواو) conjunction; (منّا المسلمون) like منّا الصالحون, and likewise (منّا القاسطون); (فمن) like the first; (أسلم) past verb in the position of a jussive, protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الفاء) linking to the answer of the condition; (تحرّوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents, and (الواو) is the agent..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا منّا المسلمون..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «منّا المسلمون» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «منّا القاسطون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.
The clause «من أسلم» has no grammatical position: resumptive and causal [Note: It may be conjoined to the khabar clause (منّا المسلمون) with the link implied, i.e. "so whoever among us submits ..."].
The clause «أسلم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «أولئك تحرّوا ...» is in the position of a jussive, the answer of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تحرّوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
15- (الواو) conjunction; (أمّا) particle of condition and detailing; (الفاء) linking to the answer of أمّا; (لجهنّم) attached to a ḥāl of (حطبا).
The clause «القاسطون.. كانوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause من أسلم..
The clause «كانوا.. حطبا» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (القاسطون).
16- (الواو) parenthetical — or resumptive; (أن) lightened from the heavy form, its noun being the pronoun of the matter, omitted; (لو) non-jussivising conditional particle; (على الطريقة) attached to (استقاموا), (اللام) occurring in the answer of لو; (ماء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لو استقاموا..) is in the position of a nominative, deputy agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أوحي إليّ".. [Note: The speech here is not the speech of the jinn but the speech of Allah the Exalted; on this basis it is permissible to conjoin it to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه استمع..), everything between them being parenthetical.]
The clause «(أوحي إليّ) أن لو ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or parenthetical, between the earlier speech of the jinn and their subsequent speech..].
The clause «the condition, its verb and its answer ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أن).
The clause «أسقيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussivising condition.
17- (اللام) the lām of causation; (نفتنهم) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; (الواو) parenthetical; (من) like the first; (عن ذكر) attached to (يعرض).. (فيه) attached to (نفتنهم). (عذابا) second mafʿūl bihi, by making نسلكه include the meaning of ندخله.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نفتنهم) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (أسقيناهم).
The clause «نفتنهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «من يعرض ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «يعرض ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «يسلكه ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
18- (الواو) conjunction; (لله) attached to the khabar of أنّ; (الفاء) linking to the answer of an implied condition; (لا) prohibitive, jussivising; (مع) adverb, accusative, attached to a ḥāl of (أحدا) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ المساجد لله) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أن لو استقاموا..).
The clause «لا تدعوا ...» is in the position of a jussive, the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have prepared yourselves for worship, then do not call ..".
19- (الواو) conjunction; (لمّا) adverb meaning "when", including the meaning of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the content of the answer..; (عليه) attached to (لبدا), by its being interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "groups"..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه لما قام..) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar, or to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه استمع ...) in verse (1) of this sūra.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its answer ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «قام عبد الله ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يدعوه ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of قام. The clause «كادوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussivising condition.
The clause «يكونون ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كادوا.

* Morphology:
(3) تعالى: in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by substitution; its origin is تعالي — with yāʾ at its end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed to alif.
(جدّ): a noun meaning greatness and majesty, with fatḥa on the jīm; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(6) رهقا: a non-analogical (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral رهق, meaning "to cover, overtake", of the class of فرح; here it means folly and transgression.
(8) حرسا: a collective noun (ism jamʿ) or the plural of حارس, active participle from the triliteral حرس; its pattern is فاعل, and the pattern of حرس is فعل with two fatḥas.
(9) رصدا: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral رصد, of the class of نصر, meaning "he watched him" or "he lay in wait for him on his way"; in the verse it is used as an intensive adjective with the meaning of the passive participle, i.e. "made ready for him, prepared".. or by implying a muḍāf, i.e. "possessing watchfulness".
(11) قددا: plural of قدّة, a noun meaning conduct and way, derived from (قدّ السير), i.e. "he cut the strap". The pattern of قدّة is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are the same letter; the pattern of قدد is فعل, with kasra then fatḥa.
(12) هربا: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral هرب, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(14) القاسطون: plural of القاسط, active participle from the triliteral قسط, meaning "he acted unjustly"; its pattern is فاعل.
(تحرّوا): in it there is iʿlāl by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescents, the lām of the word and the wāw of the plural; its pattern is تفعّوا, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ʿayn.
(15) حطبا: a collective noun; a single piece of it is حطبة, whose pattern is فعلة with two fatḥas; the plural is أحطاب on the pattern أفعال, and حطب is فعل.
(16) غدقا: ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the triliteral غدق, of the class of فرح, meaning "to give abundantly"; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(17) صعدا: maṣdar of the triliteral صعد, of the class of فرح; the maṣdar is used as an adjective with the meaning of the active participle, for intensiveness.
(19) لبدا: plural of لبدة, on the pattern of سدرة — with kasra on the lām — a noun for the hair above the neck of the lion. Anything you stick together firmly you have لبّدته. The pattern of لبد is فعل, with kasra then fatḥa, and it may take ḍamma, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: أهلكت مالا لبدا [Note: In verse (6) of Sūrat al-Balad.].

* Rhetoric:
The secret in the difference in the form of the speech: in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَأَنَّا لا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَداً». The part of the speech before «أم» has a form different from the form of what comes after it, because in the first the verb of intending is passive, and in the second the verb of intending is active.
The reason calling for that is courtesy towards Allah, Glorified and Exalted, in that they did not explicitly attribute evil to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as they explicitly did with good, even though the doer of all is Allah the Exalted.
They thus combined courtesy with soundness of belief.
The art of clarification (īḍāḥ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا الْهُدى آمَنَّا بِهِ فَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِرَبِّهِ فَلا يَخافُ بَخْساً وَلا رَهَقاً».
This art is the resolution of a difficulty arising from the apparent sense of the speech.
For Allah, Glorified and Exalted, made clear — after mentioning faith — that the believer fears no requital of loss or of injustice, because he did not defraud anyone of a right, nor did he commit (رهق) [i.e. did not cover] injustice against anyone; so he does not fear the requital of the two.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أشرك) ..
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أدعوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «لا أشرك ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أملك) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (ضرّا).], (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّي لا أملك ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «لا أملك ...» is in the position of an accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; the khabar of إنّ is in the position of a nominative.], khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:22-24.t:
* I'rab:
(من الله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجيرني), with the omission of a muḍāf; (الواو) conjunction; (من دونه) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive — or parenthetical. The clause «إنّي لن يجيرني ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «لن يجيرني.. أحد ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «لن أجد ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لن يجيرني أحد.
23- (إلّا) for exception; (بلاغا) excepted by (إلّا), accusative [Note: This exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) if البلاغ is excepted from (ملتحدا), because the conveying from Allah does not fall under His saying (لن أجد ... ملتحدا), since it is not apart from Allah.. On this basis the clause قل إنّي لن يجيرني ... is resumptive. It is also possible for the exception to be connected (muttaṣil) if what is excepted from is (الضرّ والرشد), i.e. "I possess nothing for you except a conveying from Allah"; on this basis the clause قل إنّي لن يجيرني ... is parenthetical.] (من الله) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (بلاغا), (الواو) conjunction; (رسالاته) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty, genitive like it [Note: Or conjoined to (بلاغا), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra.], (الواو) resumptive; (من) jussivising conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (الفاء) linking to the answer of the condition; (له) attached to the khabar of إنّ; (خالدين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun in (له), taking into account the plural meaning drawn from the conditional (من); (فيها) attached to (خالدين), and likewise the adverb أبدا.
The clause «من يعص ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعص ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «إنّ له نار جهنّم ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the answer of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
24- (حتّى) particle of inception (ibtidāʾ); (ما) relative noun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi; and (الواو) in (يوعدون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الفاء) linking to the answer of the condition; (السين) for mere emphasis [Note: Because seeing the punishment occurs together with the knowing, and the sīn, if it conveyed futurity, would make the knowing come later.], (من) relative noun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: It may be an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is أضعف, and the nominal clause stands in place of the object of يعلمون, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.], (أضعف) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو"; (ناصرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative; (أقلّ عددا) like أضعف ناصرا, being conjoined to it..
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يوعدون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «سيعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition.
The clause «(هو) أضعف ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(23) أبدا: an adverbial noun of time; it comes with the meaning of perpetual time, the beginningless, the ancient and the everlasting. Its plural is آباد and أبود, with ḍamma on the hamza. The adverb is mostly used for the future, in negation and affirmation; you say لا أفعله أبدا or لم أفعله أبدا. Its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:25-28.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) negative particle; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (قريب) fronted khabar (predicate), nominative [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) relying on the interrogative, and (ما) with its ṣila is an agent that stands in place of the khabar.], (ما) maṣdar particle [Note: Or a relative in the position of a nominative, the returning pronoun being omitted.], (أم) a particle equivalent to the hamza (muʿādila), conjunctive; (له) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما توعدون) is in the position of a nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن أدري ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «قريب ما توعدون ...» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of أدري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «توعدون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما), whether particle or noun.
The clause «يجعل له ربّي ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause قريب ما توعدون.
26- (عالم) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" [Note: Or a badal (substitute) of (ربّي) — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it —], (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative; (على غيبه) attached to (يظهر).
The clause «(هو) عالم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) of ربّي.].
The clause «لا يظهر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause (هو) عالم.
27- (إلّا) for exception; (من) relative noun in the position of an accusative, badal of (أحدا) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, excepted by إلّا ... And if (إلّا) means لكن, the relative is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (إنّه يسلك). It is also permissible for (من) to be a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause ارتضى and whose answer is فإنّه يسلك.], (من رسول) tamyīz (specification) of the implied pronoun that is the object of ارتضى, i.e. "He approved him as a messenger" [Note: It may be attached to a ḥāl of the implied pronoun.], (الفاء) causal [Note: Or redundant, or linking to the answer of the condition.], (من بين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسلك), and likewise (من خلفه); (رصدا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative ...
The clause «ارتضى ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «إنّه يسلك ...» has no grammatical position: causal [Note: Or in the position of a nominative, khabar of the relative من.. or in the position of a jussive, the answer of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.].
The clause «يسلك ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
28- (اللام) causal; (يعلم) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām, its agent being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "هو" [Note: There is disagreement among the exegetes over what this pronoun refers to. Some made it the pronoun of the Name of Majesty, i.e. "so that Allah may know".. some made it refer to the Messenger, upon him be peace, i.e. "so that Muḥammad may know that the messengers before him had conveyed the message".. some made it refer to the messengers, i.e. "so that the messengers may know that the angels convey".. or "so that Iblīs and the jinn may know that the messengers have conveyed the messages of their Lord".. or "so that whoever denied the messengers may know that the envoys had conveyed" ... etc.], (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted; (قد) particle of realisation; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or conjunction; (بما) attached to (أحاط), (لديهم) adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative, attached to the omitted ṣila of ما; (الواو) conjunction; (عددا) tamyīz, accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is synonymous with it, or the kind of his counting, i.e. "He reckoned it with a reckoning".].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (يسلك).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن قد أبلغوا..) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «قد أبلغوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
The clause «أحاط ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of يعلم [Note: If the pronoun of يعلم is Allah. The clause is conjoined to the clause أبلغوا if the pronoun refers to other than Allah.].
The clause «أحصى ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause أحاط, taking its i'rab.

* Morphology:
(28) أحاط: in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by substitution; its origin is أحوط on the pattern أفعل. The fatḥa was heavy on the wāw, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the ḥāʾ — iʿlāl by quiescence — then the wāw was changed to alif because the letter before it had fatḥa and it was originally vowelled — iʿlāl by substitution.
(أحصى): in it there is iʿlāl by substitution; its origin is أحصي, with yāʾ at its end — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed to alif; its pattern is أفعل.
(كلّ): a noun denoting the totality of a thing; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
